# Node reference

Every built-in node type with its inputs, outputs and params, by family. A param marked with a group, like *(more)*, sits in that folded section of the param panel. A soft range limits only the slider; typed values outside it are kept. For what the families are for, see [Concepts](../concepts.md).

Families: [tex](#tex), [chan](#chan), [table](#table), [geo](#geo), [mat](#mat), [light](#light), [view](#view), [script](#script), [out](#out), [comp](#comp), [node](#node)

### tex.blob_track

Finds people, hands or spots of light in a camera picture and follows each with an id that stays: positions to drive content with

Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (tex): The picture to search, a camera usually
- `background` (tex): The empty scene, for detect background; unconnected: learned

Outputs:

- `out` (tex): What the tracker sees, at the analysed size (`show`)
- `blobs` (table): One row per blob: id, x, y, left, top, width, height, area, age, vx, vy, r, g, b
- `chans` (chan): count, and id, x, y, area per slot (x1, y1, ...); a blob keeps its slot

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detect` | background \| bright | `"background"` |  | What counts as part of a blob; background: what differs from the empty scene (the `background` input where connected, else learned: `blob_track.learn`); bright: whatever is brighter than `threshold` |
| `threshold` | float | `0.1` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Difference to the background (in any channel), or brightness, from which a pixel counts |
| `adapt` | float | `30` | 0 to 300 s (soft) | How soon a lasting change (light, a moved chair) becomes background; someone standing still fades ten times slower; 0: never |
| `min_area` | float | `0.1` | 0 to 5 % (soft) | Smaller blobs are ignored (of the picture's area) |
| `max_area` | float | `50` | 1 to 100 % (soft) | Larger blobs are ignored (the whole room changing is not a blob) |
| `max_blobs` | int | `16` | 1 to 32 (soft) | Most blobs reported; with more found, the largest are kept |
| `show` | overlay \| mask \| difference \| background | `"overlay"` |  | What `out` shows; overlay: the picture with the blobs marked; mask: the pixels counted, white on black; difference: the difference to the background (the threshold is mid grey); background: the learned background |
| `size` *(more)* | int | `320` | 64 to 960 px (soft) | Width the input is analysed at; more finds smaller things and costs more |
| `open` *(more)* | int | `1` | 0 to 6 px (soft) | Removes specks and lines thinner than twice this (at the analysed size) |
| `close` *(more)* | int | `2` | 0 to 6 px (soft) | Fills holes and joins parts closer than twice this |
| `reach` *(more)* | float | `0.15` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | How far a blob may jump between frames and keep its id, as a share of the width. Measured from where the blob's speed puts it |
| `hold` *(more)* | float | `0.5` | 0 to 5 s (soft) | A blob gone for less keeps its id when it comes back |
| `slots` *(more)* | int | `4` | 0 to 8 (soft) | Blobs in `chans`, each as id, x, y, area with the slot's number (id 0: empty) |

### tex.blur

Softens a picture: a Gaussian blur, in every direction or only across or only up and down

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | float | `8` | 0 to 100 px (soft) | Blur radius in pixels (three standard deviations of the Gaussian); below 0.5 leaves the input as it is |
| `direction` | both \| horizontal \| vertical | `"both"` |  | Which way the picture is smeared; both: in every direction, a round blur; horizontal: only left and right, as motion across; vertical: only up and down |
| `extend` *(more)* | hold \| zero \| repeat \| mirror | `"hold"` |  | What the blur reads beyond the input's edges; hold keeps the edges from darkening; hold: the edge pixels continue outwards; zero: transparent black; repeat: the input again, tiled; mirror: the input again, mirrored, so the copies meet at the edges |

### tex.cache

Keeps the last frames of its input and shows one from a few frames back: a delay, or a moment held

Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | int | `30` | 1 to 240 f (soft) | Frames kept (at most 2 GiB of them) |
| `index` | int | `0` | 0 to 239 f (soft) | How many frames back the output is; 0 is the newest |
| `record` | bool | `true` |  | Take new frames; off holds what is kept |
| `persist` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | While not recording, keep the held frames in the state snapshots, so they survive a restart |

### tex.channel_mix

Mixes the colour channels anew: swap red and blue, make grey from one channel, turn alpha into colour

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `red` | vec4 | `[1, 0, 0, 0]` | -2 to 2 (soft) | How much of the input's r, g, b and a makes the output's red |
| `green` | vec4 | `[0, 1, 0, 0]` | -2 to 2 (soft) | How much of the input's r, g, b and a makes the output's green |
| `blue` | vec4 | `[0, 0, 1, 0]` | -2 to 2 (soft) | How much of the input's r, g, b and a makes the output's blue |
| `alpha` | vec4 | `[0, 0, 0, 1]` | -2 to 2 (soft) | How much of the input's r, g, b and a makes the output's alpha |
| `bias` *(more)* | vec4 | `[0, 0, 0, 0]` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Added to r, g, b, a afterwards |

### tex.chroma_key

Cuts out a green or blue screen: pixels near a key colour become transparent

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | colour | `[0, 1, 0, 1]` |  | The screen's colour; only its hue and saturation count, so shadows on the screen key too |
| `tolerance` | float | `0.1` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Chroma distance from the key that is fully transparent |
| `softness` | float | `0.08` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Width of the partly transparent edge beyond tolerance, in the same chroma distance |
| `spill` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | How much of the key's tint is removed from what stays |
| `invert` | bool | `false` |  | Keep the key colour, drop the rest |
| `output` | keyed \| matte | `"keyed"` |  | What the node puts out; keyed: the input with the key colour transparent and its spill removed; matte: the alpha it would get, as white (kept) on black (keyed out) |

### tex.composite

Lays up to four pictures on top of each other: over, add, multiply, screen and other blend modes

Inputs:

- `layer1` (tex): The bottom layer. The output has the size of the first connected layer
- `layer2` (tex)
- `layer3` (tex)
- `layer4` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | over \| add \| multiply \| screen \| subtract \| difference \| maximum \| minimum \| average \| inside \| outside \| atop \| overlay \| color \| luminosity | `"over"` |  | How each layer goes onto what lies below it: layer2 onto layer1, then layer3 onto that, ...; over: the layer in front, covering by its alpha; add: both summed: brighter, black adds nothing; multiply: both multiplied: darker, white changes nothing; screen: the opposite of multiply: lighter, black changes nothing; subtract: the picture below minus the layer's colour; difference: how far the colours differ, per channel; maximum: the brighter of both, per channel; minimum: the darker of both, per channel; average: half of each; inside: the layer only where the picture below is (its alpha); outside: the layer only where the picture below is not; atop: the layer over the picture below, only where that is; overlay: darkens the dark and brightens the bright parts of the picture below by the layer; color: the layer's hue and saturation at the brightness below (tinting a grey picture); luminosity: the layer's brightness with the hue and saturation below |
| `swap` | bool | `false` |  | Swap the order of each step: the picture below onto the layer (TouchDesigner's Swap Operation Order) |

### tex.constant

A picture in one colour: a background, a fill, a black to start from

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |
| `color` | colour | `[0, 0, 0, 1]` |  | The colour, linear RGBA with straight alpha; above 1 is brighter than white |

### tex.contour

Contour lines as on a map: a line wherever a channel (a height map, say) crosses a step of `interval`

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `interval` | float | `0.05` | 0.005 to 0.25 (soft) | Step in the channel's value from one line to the next |
| `offset` | float | `0` | 0 to 0.25 (soft) | Value of one of the lines; the others lie whole intervals above and below |
| `thickness` | float | `1.5` | 0.5 to 8 px (soft) | Width of the lines in pixels, the same on steep and gentle slopes |
| `smooth` | float | `0` | 0 to 16 px (soft) | Smooths a noisy height map so the lines come out calm, without islands. Radius in pixels, like tex.blur's size. Under mode over the picture itself stays sharp; 0: off |
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Colour of the lines |
| `channel` | luminance \| red \| green \| blue \| alpha | `"luminance"` |  | Channel the lines follow, on straight colour (a height map: any of the colours); luminance: the brightness as the eye weighs it (Rec. 709); red: the red channel only; green: the green channel only; blue: the blue channel only; alpha: the opacity |
| `range` *(more)* | vec2 | `[0, 1]` |  | Only values strictly between these get a line: a map clipped at 0 or 1 gets none around its flat parts |
| `mode` | lines \| alpha \| over | `"lines"` |  | What the lines are drawn on; lines: on opaque black; alpha: on transparent, to lay over a picture with tex.composite; over: over the input |

### tex.cross

Crossfades between two pictures: 0 shows a, 1 shows b

Inputs:

- `a` (tex): The output has its size
- `b` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cross` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Mix between the inputs: 0 is all a, 1 all b, 0.5 half each |

### tex.denoise

Calms a noisy picture (a camera in the dark): averages over frames where the picture is still

Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | float | `8` | 1 to 64 (soft) | About how many frames are averaged where the picture is still, for brightness noise; more is calmer; 1: off |
| `color_frames` | float | `8` | 1 to 64 (soft) | The same for colour noise (coloured speckles) |
| `motion` | float | `0.06` | 0 to 0.3 (soft) | Change above which a pixel counts as moving and shows the new frame at once. Raise it when the noise still flickers, lower it when moving things leave trails. Measured on the square root of the values, so it means about the same in dark and bright parts |
| `spatial` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Smooths the brightness of moving parts, where the average cannot help. Edges stronger than `motion` are kept; 0: off |
| `color_spatial` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | The same for the colour; the eye forgives soft colour more than soft brightness |
| `reset` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Forget the average, while on |

### tex.displace

Warps a picture by another: each pixel is pushed by the values of a map (ripples, heat haze, flow)

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)
- `map` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `horizontal` | red \| green \| blue \| alpha \| luminance \| none | `"red"` |  | Channel of the map that shifts the picture across, by weight x per unit away from midpoint; red: the map's red channel; green: the map's green channel; blue: the map's blue channel; alpha: the map's opacity; luminance: the map's brightness (Rec. 709); none: no push this way |
| `vertical` | red \| green \| blue \| alpha \| luminance \| none | `"green"` |  | Channel of the map that shifts the picture up and down, by weight y per unit away from midpoint; red: the map's red channel; green: the map's green channel; blue: the map's blue channel; alpha: the map's opacity; luminance: the map's brightness (Rec. 709); none: no push this way |
| `weight` | vec2 | `[0.1, 0.1]` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Push for a map value 1 above the midpoint, in image sizes |
| `midpoint` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Map value that does not push |
| `extend` *(more)* | hold \| zero \| repeat \| mirror | `"hold"` |  | What shows where the picture is fetched from beyond the input's edges; hold: the edge pixels continue outwards; zero: transparent black; repeat: the input again, tiled; mirror: the input again, mirrored, so the copies meet at the edges |

### tex.edge

Finds the edges in a picture and draws them as lines: outlines, a sketched look

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | float | `2` | 0 to 10 (soft) | Gain on the edge: higher makes faint edges visible and strong ones solid (clipped at 1) |
| `distance` | float | `1` | 0.5 to 8 px (soft) | Distance of the neighbours compared; larger finds broader, softer edges |
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Colour of the edges |
| `mode` | edges \| alpha \| over | `"edges"` |  | What the edges are drawn on; edges: on opaque black; alpha: on transparent, to lay over something else; over: over the input |

### tex.feedback

Feeds a chain's result back into it the next frame: trails, echoes, patterns that grow. Wire the end of the chain into `previous`

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `initial` (tex): Passed on until `previous` has a frame, and while `reset` is on: what the loop starts from
- `previous` (tex) Sees the previous frame, so it may close a loop.

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reset` | bool | `false` |  | Pass `initial` instead, while on |
| `persist` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | Keep the loop's last frame in the state snapshots, so a restart carries on from it |

### tex.fit

Fits a picture into a frame of another size or shape: whole with bars, cropped to fill, or stretched

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the output in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the output in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |
| `fit` | fit \| fill \| stretch \| native | `"fit"` |  | How the input sits in the frame; fit: whole and as large as fits, aspect kept; bars where it does not fill; fill: covering the frame, aspect kept; what sticks out is cropped; stretch: covering the frame, distorted to its aspect; native: pixel for pixel, unscaled |
| `justify` | vec2 | `[0.5, 0.5]` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Where the image sits in the frame: 0 left or top, 1 right or bottom |
| `extend` | zero \| hold \| repeat \| mirror | `"zero"` |  | What fills the frame where the input does not reach (the bars of fit or native); zero: transparent black; hold: the input's edge pixels continue outwards; repeat: the input again, tiled; mirror: the input again, mirrored, so the copies meet at the edges |

### tex.flip

Mirrors a picture left to right or top to bottom, or turns its rows into columns

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flip_x` | bool | `false` |  | Mirror left to right: the left edge becomes the right |
| `flip_y` | bool | `false` |  | Mirror top to bottom: the top edge becomes the bottom |
| `flop` | bool | `false` |  | Swap the axes (transpose); the output is as wide as the input is high |

### tex.fluid

A simulated fluid like smoke or ink: motion (a camera's, tracked hands) stirs it and colour flows along

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `force` (tex): Motion that pushes the fluid: tex.optical_flow's output as it is. Red x in widths, green y in heights, down positive, per input frame
- `dye` (tex): Colour poured in, where `inject` says. Unwired: `color` where the fluid moves
- `obstacles` (tex): Solid where brighter than half: the fluid flows around it
- `splats` (table): Pushes and dye at points, one per row, at most 64: tex.blob_track's table as it is. Columns x, y (0 to 1, from the top left); optional vx, vy (image sizes per second), r, g, b and radius (image heights)

Outputs:

- `out` (tex): The dye, at width x height
- `velocity` (tex): The fluid's velocity at the grid's size: red x in widths, green y in heights, down positive, per second. tex.displace with midpoint 0 moves a picture along it

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |
| `force` | float | `4` | 0 to 20 (soft) | How strongly motion (the force input and the splats) pushes the fluid. Per second, this many times the motion's speed is added to the fluid's speed |
| `velocity_fade` | float | `2` | 0.05 to 30 s (soft) | Time in which the fluid loses half its speed; longer keeps it swirling |
| `dye_fade` | float | `3` | 0.05 to 60 s (soft) | Time in which the dye loses half its strength |
| `inject` | moving \| everywhere | `"moving"` |  | Where dye comes in; moving: where the force input or a splat moves, the faster the more; the dye input's colours, or `color` while the dye input is unwired; everywhere: the dye input everywhere, splats whether they move or not |
| `amount` | float | `4` | 0 to 30 (soft) | How fast the dye takes on the poured colour, per second, where the fluid moves fast. At 4, about two thirds in a quarter of a second. Pouring paints over, so the dye never gets brighter than the poured colour |
| `color` | colour | `[0.35, 0.7, 1, 1]` |  | Colour of the dye while the dye input is unwired, and of splats without r, g, b columns. The colour's alpha slows the pouring |
| `vorticity` | float | `0.3` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Brings back the small swirls the coarse grid smooths away; 0: off |
| `viscosity` *(more)* | float | `0` | 0 to 0.01 (soft) | Thickness, honey instead of smoke: neighbouring parts take on each other's motion. In image heights squared per second; 0: off, costs nothing |
| `size` *(more)* | int | `256` | 64 to 512 px (soft) | Width of the simulation grid; the height follows the picture's shape. More gives finer swirls and costs more. The dye keeps the output's size |
| `iterations` *(more)* | int | `20` | 4 to 60 (soft) | Steps that keep the fluid from being squeezed together. Fewer cost less and let the fluid bulge and leak |
| `splat_radius` *(more)* | float | `0.05` | 0.005 to 0.3 (soft) | Radius of a splat from the table without a radius column, in image heights |
| `edges` *(more)* | walls \| open | `"walls"` |  | What the picture's edges are to the fluid; walls: the fluid turns along them; open: the fluid flows out, with the dye |
| `reset` | bool | `false` |  | Starts over from a still fluid without dye, every frame while on |
| `persist` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | Keep velocity and dye in the state snapshots, so a restart carries on from them |

### tex.from_chan

Turns channels into a picture: a row per channel, a pixel per sample. Numbers for shaders and geo.tex_instance

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layout` | auto \| rows \| rgba | `"auto"` |  | How the channels become pixels; auto: rgba when the channels are exactly r, g, b (and a), as chan.from_tex names them, else rows; rows: one grey row per channel, as many pixels wide as there are samples; rgba: the first four channels as red, green, blue and alpha of one row (alpha 1 where missing) |
| `low` | float | `0` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Channel value that becomes black (0); lower values go below 0 |
| `high` | float | `1` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Channel value that becomes white (1); higher values go above 1 |

### tex.hsv

Turns the colours round the colour wheel and makes them more vivid or paler, brighter or darker

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hue` | float | `0` | -180 to 180° (soft) | Added to the hue: 120 turns red into green. Any angle works, the hue wraps around |
| `saturation` | float | `1` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Multiplies the saturation: 0 is grey, 1 unchanged, 2 more vivid (clipped at full) |
| `value` | float | `1` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Multiplies the value (the brightest channel): 0 is black, 2 twice as bright |

### tex.lens_distort

Bends a picture as a lens does (barrel or pincushion), or straightens what a lens bent

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k1` | float | `0.1` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Main term; positive pulls the edges in (barrel), negative pushes them out |
| `k2` | float | `0` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Fourth-order term, for the far edges |
| `scale` | float | `1` | 0.25 to 4 (soft) | Zoom after the distortion: above 1 enlarges and hides the edges that barrel distortion pulls in |
| `center` *(more)* | vec2 | `[0.5, 0.5]` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Optical centre; 0, 0 is the top left |
| `extend` | hold \| zero \| repeat \| mirror | `"zero"` |  | What shows where the picture is fetched from beyond the input's edges; hold: the edge pixels continue outwards; zero: transparent black; repeat: the input again, tiled; mirror: the input again, mirrored, so the copies meet at the edges |

### tex.level

Adjusts black and white, gamma, contrast and brightness, inverts, or fades a picture out

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `black` | float | `0` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Input value that becomes 0, per channel; darker goes below 0. The first step |
| `white` | float | `1` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Input value that becomes 1, per channel; brighter goes above 1 (not clipped) |
| `gamma` | float | `1` | 0.01 to 10 | Bends the midtones after black and white: above 1 brightens them, below 1 darkens; 0 and 1 stay |
| `contrast` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Spreads values away from mid grey (0.5) after gamma: 0 is flat grey, 2 doubles the distance |
| `brightness` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Multiplies the colour after contrast: 0 is black, 2 twice as bright |
| `invert` | bool | `false` |  | 1 minus the colour, after all the steps above; alpha stays |
| `opacity` | float | `1` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Multiplies alpha: 0 transparent, 1 as the input; fades a layer in a composite |

### tex.limit

Keeps values within a range: clips them, or wraps or mirrors them back in (a ramp becomes repeating stripes)

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min` | float | `0` | -1 to 2 (soft) | Lowest value kept, per channel of the straight colour |
| `max` | float | `1` | -1 to 2 (soft) | Highest value kept; at or below min everything becomes min |
| `mode` | clamp \| wrap \| mirror | `"clamp"` |  | What happens to values outside min to max; clamp: they stop at min or max; wrap: they start again from min: a ramp becomes a sawtooth; mirror: they turn back: a ramp becomes a triangle wave |
| `alpha` | bool | `false` |  | Limit alpha the same way; off keeps the input's alpha |

Recolours a picture through a strip of colours: brightness picks the colour (a gradient map), or a curve per channel

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | luminance \| channels | `"luminance"` |  | Which input values pick the place in the lookup row (0 its left end, 1 its right); luminance: the brightness picks one colour of the row (a gradient map); channels: red, green and blue each through the row's own channel (a curve per channel) |
| `row` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Height in the lookup texture that is read; 0 is the top |

Fits a part of the content onto one projector: corner pinning, mesh warp, soft edges where projectors overlap

Inputs:

| `fit` | fit \| fill \| stretch | `"fit"` |  | How the region sits in the picture before the corners move; fit: whole, aspect kept, with bars; fill: covering the picture, aspect kept, cropped; stretch: covering the picture, distorted to its aspect |
| `blend` | bool | `true` |  | Soft edges where other mappers of the same input overlap this one (off for stacked projectors) |
| `pattern` | bool | `false` |  | An alignment grid of the input instead of the picture |
| `corner_tl` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Top left corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes (drag it in the viewer) |
| `corner_tr` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Top right corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes |
| `corner_br` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Bottom right corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes |
| `corner_bl` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Bottom left corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes |
| `warp` *(warp)* | text |  |  | Mesh warp: one line per grid row, `dx,dy` offsets in picture sizes; empty is none (edit it in the viewer) |
| `blend_gamma` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0.2 to 3 (soft) | Exponent on the soft edge; above 1 darkens the overlap, below 1 brightens it |

| `invert` | bool | `false` |  | Black shows a, white b |

Makes a picture grey: by brightness, by the average or the brightest channel, or from one channel

Inputs:

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | luminance \| average \| maximum \| red \| green \| blue \| alpha | `"luminance"` |  | How the grey is made from the colour; luminance: brightness as the eye weighs it (Rec. 709): green counts most, blue least; average: red, green and blue equally; maximum: the brightest of red, green and blue; red: the red channel only; green: the green channel only; blue: the blue channel only; alpha: the opacity, as grey |
| `opaque` | bool | `false` |  | Alpha 1 instead of the input's |

A picture (and sound) from another program or computer on the network, through NDI®; needs the NDI runtime (ndi.video)

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | text |  |  | The source's name as `PC (Source)` or a part of it, e.g. `OBS` (the ... menu lists those on the network); empty: the first source |
| `bandwidth` | full \| low | `"full"` |  | Which of the sender's streams to take; full: the stream as sent; low: a smaller, lower-quality stream the sender offers beside it, for previews |
| `alpha` | straight \| premultiplied \| opaque | `"straight"` |  | How the source's transparency is taken (NDI's alpha is straight); straight: colour and alpha apart, as most programs take it; premultiplied: colour multiplied by alpha; opaque: no transparency: sent over black, or a received alpha ignored |

### tex.noise

Cloudy random patterns, still or slowly changing: textures, masks, organic motion for a displacement

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |
| `basis` | gradient \| value | `"gradient"` |  | The kind of noise each octave is made of; gradient: smooth, round blobs (Perlin-like); value: blockier, with a visible grid of cells |
| `seed` | int | `0` | 0 to 100 (soft) | Picks another noise of the same look; each number gives the same picture every time |
| `frequency` | float | `4` | 0.1 to 100 (soft) | Size of the pattern: noise cells per image height; higher is finer |
| `octaves` | int | `3` | 1 to 8 | Layers of ever finer noise added up (fractal detail); 1 is smooth blobs only |
| `roughness` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Strength of each octave relative to the one before; higher gives more fine grain |
| `lacunarity` *(more)* | float | `2` | 1 to 4 (soft) | How much finer each octave is than the one before (2: twice the cells) |
| `amplitude` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Contrast: the noise (about -1 to 1) is multiplied by this, then offset is added |
| `offset` | float | `0.5` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Added after amplitude: the mean grey. With 0.5 and 0.5 the values span about 0 to 1 |
| `speed` | float | `0` | 0 to 4 (soft) | How fast the pattern morphs, in cells per second; 0 is still. The noise moves through a third dimension, so the picture does not slide |
| `translate` *(more)* | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` |  | Position in the noise, in cells: x and y slide the picture, z morphs it as speed does |
| `color` | bool | `false` |  | Three independent channels instead of grey |
| `alpha` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0 to 1 | Opacity of the whole picture; below 1, what lies under it in a composite shows through |

Passes its input on unchanged: a fixed point to look at, or for other nodes to refer to while the chain before it changes

### tex.optical_flow

Measures how each part of the picture moves from frame to frame: motion to stir a fluid or drive a displacement

Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `colors` | bool | `false` |  | Show the motion as colours: direction as hue, speed as brightness. For looking at the motion; nodes that use the motion want this off |
| `confidence` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Blue says how well the motion is pinned down, 0 to 1: high where there is texture (moving or not), low on a plain wall. Off: blue is 0, and a still picture is black |
| `fill` | int | `4` | 0 to 6 (soft) | Rounds of filling in. Motion found at edges and texture spreads into plain parts of the same thing (skin, a shirt) and stops at edges. Each round reaches twice as far; 0: off |
| `threshold` | float | `0.25` | 0 to 4 px (soft) | Slower motion than this fades out, so camera noise does not shimmer. In pixels per frame at the analysed size; below half of it nothing is left |
| `size` *(more)* | int | `320` | 64 to 960 px (soft) | Width the input is analysed at, and the output's; more sees finer motion and costs more |
| `levels` *(more)* | int | `4` | 1 to 6 (soft) | Pyramid levels, each half the size of the one before; each one doubles the fastest motion followed |
| `iterations` *(more)* | int | `3` | 1 to 6 (soft) | Refining steps per level; more is more exact and costs more |
| `window` *(more)* | int | `3` | 1 to 6 px (soft) | Radius of the neighbourhood each pixel's motion is judged from; more is smoother and steadier, less keeps small moving things apart |

Inside a component: one of its outputs.

- `in` (tex)

### tex.quantize

Fewer colours and bigger pixels: posterised, banded or retro pixel looks

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `levels` | int | `4` | 2 to 32 (soft) | Values per channel, black and white included |
| `block` | int | `1` | 1 to 64 px (soft) | Side of the square blocks that take one colour; 1 keeps every pixel |
| `dither` | none \| ordered | `"none"` |  | How values between two levels are shown; none: each snaps to the nearest level: hard bands; ordered: a 4 x 4 Bayer pattern per block mixes the two levels, so gradients survive few levels |
| `space` *(more)* | perceptual \| linear | `"perceptual"` |  | Where the levels are evenly spaced; perceptual: to the eye (on the sRGB curve): even steps from black to white; linear: in linear light: most levels look bright, few dark |
| `alpha` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Snap alpha to the levels too; off keeps the input's alpha, so soft edges stay soft |

### tex.render

Renders 3D geometry through a camera into a picture, with a second picture of data for shaders and masks

Inputs:

- `geo` (geo): What to render
- `texture` (tex): Put on the geometry when `surface` is texture or auto
- `lights` (light): Without lights, phong materials are black
- `camera` (view): A view.camera; needed

Outputs:

- `out` (tex): The rendered picture
- `data` (tex): Texture coordinates in red and green, part id + 1 in blue (0 where nothing was drawn), distance along the view in metres in alpha. Data for shaders and masks, not something to look at

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |
| `surface` | auto \| material \| texture \| parts \| uv \| normals | `"auto"` |  | What the geometry is coloured with; auto: the texture input where connected, else material; material: the material put on by geo.assign_material; without one, each part's material from the file (colour times texture), unlit; texture: the texture input, by the mesh's texture coordinates, shaded by the material; parts: a colour per part id, to tell the parts apart; uv: the texture coordinates as red and green, to check an unwrap; normals: which way each point faces, as a colour |
| `background` | colour | `[0, 0, 0, 0]` |  | Colour where no geometry is drawn; the default is transparent black |
| `antialias` | bool | `true` |  | Four samples per pixel for smooth edges; off is faster and shows stair steps |
| `cull` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Leave out faces turned away (counter-clockwise is the front) |
| `shadow_size` *(more)* | int | `2048` | 256 to 4096 (soft) | Texels across each light's shadow map; more gives sharper shadows and takes more memory |
| `ao` *(occlusion)* | bool | `false` |  | Ambient occlusion: less ambient and environment light in creases and where objects meet; direct light and unlit surfaces stay as they are |
| `ao_radius` *(occlusion)* | float | `0.5` | 0.01 to 2 m (soft) | How far around a point geometry darkens it |
| `ao_strength` *(occlusion)* | float | `1` | 0 to 3 (soft) | How much of the hidden ambient light is taken away: 1 as estimated, 0.3 at most 30 %, above 1 darker |

### tex.scan

Measures with a camera what a projector lights (structured light) and keeps the result until the next scan: maps to put content onto real objects

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `proj_to_cam` (tex): Projector size: per projector pixel, the camera position in red and green (0 to 1). Blue: 1 measured, 0.5 filled in, -1 none; -1 everywhere before a scan. Use as tex.remap's map with the camera's picture as in
- `weight` (tex): Projector size: the blend weight against the other projectors of the run; multiply the projector's picture by it. 1 everywhere for a projector alone, or before a blend
- `scene` (tex): Projector size: the scene as the projector sees it (black before a scan)

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `projector` | text |  |  | The out.projector scanned (a path, or a name beside this node) |
| `camera` | text |  |  | The tex.video_in that films the projectors; the scan button scans every tex.scan naming the same camera |
| `folder` | text | `"scan"` |  | Where scans go, relative to the project. Inside, the projector's scan is the folder named after the projector's path |
| `mapper` | text |  |  | The tex.mapper feeding the projector. When every tex.scan of a run names its mapper, the run lines the mappers up (scan.align) |
| `smooth` | bool | `true` |  | proj_to_cam is the map smoothed within the decoded area, for clean remapped edges. The run's blend writes the smoothed map. Off: the map as decoded |
| `settle` *(more)* | float | `0.05` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Seconds waited past the measured light-to-camera latency before a picture is taken |
| `level` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0.05 to 1 | Brightness of the lit stripes; lower it only if the camera clips even with its exposure turned down |
| `second_level` *(more)* | float | `0` | 0 to 1 | A second pass at this brightness, merged per camera pixel with the first, the surer decode winning: a dimmer one decodes where the first clips (white surfaces, highlights). 0: one pass |
| `fill` *(more)* | int | `32` | 0 to 128 (soft) | Projector pixels the decode fills in from measured neighbours |

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | pulse \| chase \| ripple \| fill | `"pulse"` |  | What each shape shows; pulse: the whole shape fades up and down; chase: lit segments run clockwise along the outline; ripple: rings run inwards from the edge; fill: the shape in its colour, still |

| `duty` | float | `0.3` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Chase and ripple: lit part of each segment or ring |
| `softness` *(more)* | float | `0.3` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Chase and ripple: how soft the ends of segments and rings are; 0 hard |

### tex.shapes

Shapes drawn on the surface (rectangles, ellipses, polygons) with tags: masks and outlines to light parts of a facade or object on their own

Inputs:

- `table` (table): Shapes from a table (as the `table` output has them) instead of the node's own
- `trace` (tex): A mask or label picture whose regions become shapes tagged `trace_tag`, besides the node's own: traced again whenever the picture or a `trace_*` param changes, never stored. Meant for a picture that holds still (a tex.image, a shader on images); it is stretched to the surface

Outputs:

- `mask` (tex): White inside the shapes of the tags in `tag`
- `sdf` (tex): Signed distance to the edge of those shapes
- `outline` (tex): Outlines of all shapes in their tag colours, to see them while placing them
- `table` (table): Every shape as a row; another tex.shapes can read it at its `table` input
- `id` (tex): Per pixel, the shape (of the tags in `tag`) the pixel is inside, else the nearest shape. Red: the shape's id (the table's `id`). Green: a random value 0..1 per shape. Blue: where along the outline, 0..1 clockwise. Alpha: signed distance to the edge in pixels. Data for tex.shape_content, not something to look at

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the surface in pixels (the mappers' input); shape coordinates are in these pixels |
| `height` | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the surface in pixels; shape coordinates are in these pixels |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |
| `shapes` | text |  |  | One per line: `tag rect x,y w,h`, `tag ellipse x,y w,h` or `tag poly x,y x,y ...`, optionally `repeat CxR dx,dy`; surface coordinates (draw them in the viewer) |
| `tag` | text |  |  | Tags in the mask and the distance field, separated by spaces; empty: all |
| `outline` *(more)* | float | `2` | 0.5 to 8 px (soft) | Width of the lines in the outline output, in surface pixels |
| `trace_tag` *(trace)* | text | `"trace"` |  | Tag of the shapes traced from the `trace` input (one word: letters, digits, `_`) |
| `trace_channel` *(trace)* | auto \| red \| green \| blue \| alpha \| luma | `"auto"` |  | The channel of the `trace` input that is traced; auto: alpha when the picture has transparent pixels, else luma; red: the red channel (label pictures often keep their labels there); green: the green channel; blue: the blue channel; alpha: the alpha channel; luma: the brightness (Rec. 709 weights on the linear values) |
| `trace_threshold` *(trace)* | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Inside a shape is above this value (below with `trace_invert`); not used with `trace_labels` |
| `trace_invert` *(trace)* | bool | `false` |  | Inside is below the threshold: dark objects on a bright wall |
| `trace_labels` *(trace)* | bool | `false` |  | A label picture: every value above 0 is a region of its own (one shape per label), 0 is the background; the threshold is not used |
| `trace_tolerance` *(trace)* | float | `1` | 0 to 8 px (soft) | How far a traced line may stray from the pixel edges to save points, in pixels of the picture |
| `trace_min_area` *(trace)* | float | `64` | 0 to 10000 (soft) | Regions of fewer pixels of the picture are specks and dropped; holes in regions are filled |

### tex.slope

How steeply a height map or picture rises, left to right in red and top to bottom in green: relief, or a map for tex.displace

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | luminance \| red \| green \| blue \| alpha | `"luminance"` |  | Channel whose slope is measured; luminance: the brightness as the eye weighs it (Rec. 709); red: the red channel only; green: the green channel only; blue: the blue channel only; alpha: the opacity |
| `strength` | float | `4` | 0 to 50 (soft) | Gain on the slope (value change per pixel); higher makes gentle slopes visible |
| `offset` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Value of a flat area; rising slopes lie above it, falling below. 0.5 suits tex.displace's midpoint |

### tex.spout_in

A picture from another program on this machine, through Spout (Windows)

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (tex): The sender's picture, at its size

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sender` | text |  |  | The sender's name (the ... menu lists those running); empty: the active sender, the one picked last in a Spout program, else the first |
| `alpha` | straight \| premultiplied \| opaque | `"straight"` |  | How the sender's transparency is taken; straight: colour and alpha apart, as most programs take it; premultiplied: colour multiplied by alpha; opaque: no transparency: sent over black, or a received alpha ignored |

### tex.switch

Chooses which of up to eight pictures goes out: cut between scenes or looks, or crossfade

Inputs:

- `in0` (tex)
- `in1` (tex)
- `in2` (tex)
- `in3` (tex)
- `in4` (tex)
- `in5` (tex)
- `in6` (tex)
- `in7` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | float | `0` | 0 to 7 (soft) | Which input goes out: the wired inputs counted from 0, gaps skipped. Past the last: the last |
| `blend` | bool | `false` |  | Crossfade: a fractional index mixes the inputs either side (1.25: a quarter of the next). Off: it rounds down |
| `inactive` | cook \| skip | `"cook"` |  | Whether the chains not shown keep running (switching is instant) or pause (they cost nothing); cook: their chains keep cooking as if shown; skip: only the shown input's chain cooks; the other chains stand still and cost nothing. Switching to a skipped input cooks its chain in that frame: a slow chain makes the frame late, a video may need a moment to catch up. A feedback loop, cache or time machine in a skipped chain carries on from where it stopped. An input counts as connected as soon as it is wired |

### tex.text

Writes text into a picture, in an installed font or a bundled one

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | text | `"Text"` |  | What is written. Line breaks are kept; align sets how the lines line up |
| `size` | float | `100` | 4 to 500 px (soft) | Font size in pixels of the output picture (the font's em, a little more than a capital's height) |
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Colour of the text, linear RGBA with straight alpha; the rest is transparent |
| `position` | vec2 | `[0.5, 0.5]` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Where the text's anchor sits, in image sizes; 0, 0 is the top left |
| `align` | center \| left \| right | `"center"` |  | How the lines line up with each other, and which point of the block sits at position; center: centred; the block's centre at position; left: flush left; the block's left edge at position; right: flush right; the block's right edge at position |
| `font` | text | `"Inter"` |  | Family name; Inter, JetBrains Mono, Noto Serif are bundled |
| `style` | text | `"Regular"` |  | Style within the family: Regular, Bold, Italic, Light, ... The menu lists the family's styles |
| `width` *(more)* | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` *(more)* | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the picture made, in pixels; res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves width and height alone. For a deliberate resolution: a simulation, a pixel look |

### tex.threshold

A mask from brightness: white where a channel is above a value, black or transparent elsewhere

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `threshold` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Value of the channel from which a pixel passes (on straight colour) |
| `soft` | float | `0` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Width of a soft ramp above the threshold |
| `channel` | luminance \| red \| green \| blue \| alpha | `"luminance"` |  | Channel compared with the threshold; luminance: the brightness as the eye weighs it (Rec. 709); red: the red channel only; green: the green channel only; blue: the blue channel only; alpha: the opacity |
| `invert` | bool | `false` |  | Pass what lies below the threshold instead |
| `output` | mask \| alpha | `"mask"` |  | What the node puts out; mask: white where a pixel passes, black elsewhere; alpha: the input where it passes, transparent elsewhere |

### tex.tile

Repeats a picture as a grid of smaller copies, at the input's size

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repeat` | vec2 | `[2, 2]` | 1 to 16 (soft) | Copies across and down, each shrunk to fit; fractions show part of a copy |
| `mirror` | bool | `false` |  | Every other copy mirrored, so edges meet |
| `offset` *(more)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Shifts the pattern, in tiles: 0.5 moves it by half a copy |

### tex.time_machine

Shows each pixel from another moment in the past, as a map says: time smears, slit scans, echoes

Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)
- `map` (tex): Per pixel, how far back: black is now, white `length` frames ago; unconnected: `offset` alone

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | int | `120` | 1 to 1800 f (soft) | How far back white reaches, in input frames (a camera at 30 fps: 600 are 20 s) |
| `offset` | float | `0` | 0 to 600 f (soft) | Frames back added everywhere; without a map, the delay of the whole picture |
| `blend` | bool | `true` |  | Mixes the two frames nearest to the map's value. Off takes the nearer frame alone: sharper, but a smooth map shows steps |
| `scale` | float | `1` | 0.1 to 1 (soft) | Resolution of the kept frames relative to the input; 0.5 needs a quarter of the memory |
| `precision` | 16bit \| 8bit | `"16bit"` |  | How the kept frames are stored; 16bit: as they come; 8bit: in half the memory, with values above 1 clipped |
| `step` | int | `1` | 1 to 8 (soft) | Keeps only every n-th input frame: n times the length in the same memory. Between kept frames the picture is blended, and fast motion smears |
| `record` | bool | `true` |  | Take new frames; off holds what is kept |
| `budget` *(more)* | float | `0` (automatic) | 0 to 20 (soft) | Most GPU memory the kept frames take, in GiB; automatic: half of what the GPU grants penumbra. Over the budget or over what the GPU has free, fewer frames are kept, with a warning; 0: automatic |

### tex.transform

Moves, turns and scales a picture within its own frame

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translate` | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Shift in image sizes: 1 moves by the whole width or height; positive y moves down |
| `rotate` | float | `0` | -180 to 180° (soft) | Turn around the pivot, counter-clockwise on screen |
| `scale` | vec2 | `[1, 1]` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Size across and down, around the pivot: 1 keeps it, 2 doubles it, negative mirrors |
| `pivot` *(more)* | vec2 | `[0.5, 0.5]` | 0 to 1 (soft) | The point rotate and scale turn and grow around, in image sizes: 0, 0 is the top left, 0.5, 0.5 the centre |
| `extend` | hold \| zero \| repeat \| mirror | `"hold"` |  | What shows where the picture is fetched from beyond the input's edges; hold: the edge pixels continue outwards; zero: transparent black; repeat: the input again, tiled; mirror: the input again, mirrored, so the copies meet at the edges |

Plays a video file or animated GIF, looping without a gap

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs: none.

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | file (mp4, m4v, mov, mkv, webm, mxf, ts, m2ts, mts, mpg, mpeg, m2v, gif) |  |  | MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, MXF, MPEG (H.264, HEVC, ProRes, DNxHR, VP9, AV1, HAP) or GIF |
| `play` | bool | `true` |  | Off holds the current frame |
| `speed` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Playback rate; every frame is still decoded, so high speeds cost CPU |
| `loop` | bool | `true` |  | Off stops on the last frame |
| `start` *(more)* | float | `0` | 0 to 60 s (soft) | Where playback begins when the file is (re)loaded |

A live camera or capture card

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `mode` | text |  |  | Size, rate and pixel format, each optional, e.g. `1920x1080@60 NV12` or `@30`; empty: the largest, fastest the camera offers |
| `range` *(more)* | auto \| limited \| full | `"auto"` |  | Whether black is 16 or 0 in the camera's Y'CbCr. Raised blacks mean the camera sends full range while limited is assumed: pick full; auto: believe the camera (limited when it does not say); limited: black is 16, white 235 (video range); full: black is 0, white 255 |

### chan.audio_analysis

Listens to sound and turns it into numbers to animate with: loudness, bass, mid and treble, hits, tempo and beat

Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `audio` (chan)

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): Channels to bind: level, low, mid, high, onset, kick, tick, bpm, confidence, beat, bar, bar_beat; also rms, peak, and beats_per_bar, low_hz, high_hz as the params set them
- `spectrum` (chan): One channel whose samples are log-spaced bands from 30 Hz to 16 kHz
- `meters` (tex): The meters as in the viewer, on transparent black: level and band bars with peaks, tempo, beat light, bar, hits, spectrum. Drawn only while something reads this output

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | text |  |  | The channel to analyse, e.g. `ch1`; empty: all mixed |
| `offset` | float | `0` | -200 to 200 (soft) | Milliseconds to move beat and bar ahead by, to make up for the projector's delay |
| `beats_per_bar` | int | `4` | 2 to 8 (soft) | Beats in one bar (4 for 4/4, 3 for a waltz): how often bar and bar_beat come round |
| `sensitivity` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 | How readily an onset or kick counts: higher finds quieter ones |
| `min_bpm` *(more)* | float | `70` | 40 to 200 (soft) | The slowest tempo considered, in beats per minute. Keep min_bpm and max_bpm less than an octave apart: then a half or double tempo cannot be taken |
| `max_bpm` *(more)* | float | `180` | 80 to 300 (soft) | The fastest tempo considered, in beats per minute; see min_bpm |
| `normalize` | bool | `true` |  | A quiet input still spans 0 to 1: levels and spectrum are measured relative to the loudest of the last seconds |
| `floor` *(levels)* | float | `-60` | -90 to -20 dB (soft) | Quieter than this counts as silence and is not raised by normalize |
| `low` *(levels)* | float | `150` | 40 to 500 Hz (soft) | Where the low band ends: the low channel is the level below this frequency |
| `high` *(levels)* | float | `2500` | 1000 to 8000 Hz (soft) | Where the high band starts: the high channel is the level above this frequency. The mid channel covers the band between low and high |
| `bands` *(levels)* | int | `32` | 4 to 128 (soft) | Bands of the spectrum output, log-spaced from 30 Hz to 16 kHz: its samples per frame |
| `width` *(meters)* | int | `1920` | 1 to 16384 px | Width of the meters output in pixels. res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `height` *(meters)* | int | `1080` | 1 to 16384 px | Height of the meters output in pixels. res.optimize may change it to what the projectors need, unless keep_size is on |
| `keep_size` *(meters)* | bool | `false` |  | res.optimize leaves the width and height of the meters output alone |

### chan.audio_in

Sound from a microphone or audio interface, for chan.audio_analysis: one channel per input channel

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | text |  |  | Part of the input's name (Helpers > Audio lists them), e.g. `Focusrite`; empty: the system's default input |

### chan.clock

A stopwatch: counts seconds from when `run` turns on, once, looping or on and on. Gives each piece of a show a clock that starts with it

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over. Cooks in every frame, whether anything shows it or not, so it sees every change of its params.

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): `seconds` since it was switched on (once: at most `length`; loop: within the round), `fraction` of `length` (0 to 1 for once and loop), `done` (1 once a full length has passed since it was switched on, else 0). It cooks in every frame, shown or not, so it sees `run` turn off while its piece is not shown; a seek back starts it over

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | float | `1` | 0 to 1 (soft) | On from 0.5 up (with `equals` set: while it equals that number). Each time it turns on the clock starts over from 0; while it is off the clock stands at 0. Bind it to a key's gate, or to the piece channel with `equals` |
| `equals` | int | `-1` (off) | -1 to 20 (soft) | When set, `run` is on while it equals this number: bind `run` to the channel that says which piece plays and set this to the piece's number. While off, `run` is on from 0.5 up; -1: off |
| `length` | float | `10` | 0.1 to 120 s (soft) | How long one run (once) or one round (loop) takes; `fraction` is the time over it |
| `mode` | once \| loop \| free | `"once"` |  | What the clock does once `length` has passed; once: it stops at the end and holds there; loop: it starts over from 0, round after round; free: it runs on: seconds grow without end, fraction past 1 |

### chan.constant

Numbers set by hand, each a named channel: values to bind params to, one setting that drives several things

Declares further params per node, from its file or code.

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value0` | float | `0` | -1 to 1 (soft) | The channel's value; the slider spans -1 to 1, any number can be typed |
| `name0` | text | `"chan0"` |  | Name of the channel this row makes, as other nodes and bindings see it |
| `rows` *(more)* | int | `1` | 1 to 64 | How many rows; row k is the params `name<k>` and `value<k>`, counted from 0 |

### chan.dmx_in

DMX from a lighting desk over the network (Art-Net or sACN): each slot a channel to drive content with

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): ch1 to chN: the slots from `address` on, the last values held

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | art_net \| sacn | `"art_net"` |  | What the sender speaks; art_net: Art-Net, sent to this machine or as a broadcast; sacn: sACN (E1.31), to the universe's multicast group or to this machine |
| `universe` | int | `1` | 0 to 16 (soft) | Universe of the first slot, as the protocol counts (Art-Net from 0, sACN from 1); channels past its end read on in the next |
| `address` | int | `1` | 1 to 512 (soft) | DMX address (slot, from 1) that becomes ch1 |
| `count` | int | `512` | 1 to 512 (soft) | Channels made: ch1 is slot `address`, ch2 the next and so on |
| `values` | unit \| byte | `"unit"` |  | What the channels hold; unit: 0 to 1, from 0 to 255; byte: 0 to 255, as the slots are |
| `interface` *(more)* | text |  |  | IP address of this machine's network card to listen on; empty listens on all (sACN multicast then joins on the system's default one) |
| `port` *(more)* | int | `0` (the protocol's port) | 1024 to 65535 (soft) | UDP port to listen on; 0 is the protocol's own (Art-Net 6454, sACN 5568); 0: the protocol's port |

Smooths jumpy numbers over time, at their own pace up and down: calms a sensor, softens a jump

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rise` | float | `0.2` | 0 to 5 s (soft) | Time to cover 63 % of a step up; 0 follows at once |
| `fall` | float | `0.2` | 0 to 5 s (soft) | Time to cover 63 % of a step down |

### chan.from_tex

Turns a picture into numbers: its average colour, or the colours of a few areas, as channels to drive things with

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | int | `1` | 1 to 256 (soft) | Samples per channel: the picture is averaged down to this many columns |
| `rows` | int | `1` | 1 to 64 (soft) | Rows the picture is averaged down to. With more than one row, the channels are numbered by row from the top (r0, r1, ...) |
| `components` | rgba \| rgb \| red \| luminance | `"rgba"` |  | Which channels a row gives; values are linear and premultiplied, as the picture holds them; rgba: r, g, b and a; rgb: r, g and b; red: r only; luminance: lum, the brightness as the eye weighs it (Rec. 709) |

An input port of the component this node sits in: what is wired to that port outside comes out here

Inside a component: one of its inputs.

Keys of the keyboard as channels, to switch scenes or trigger things by hand during a show (while a penumbra window has the focus)

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` | text | `"1 2 3 4"` |  | Space-separated keys: digits (the number pad's too), letters, f1 to f12, space, left right up down, enter tab backspace delete insert home end pageup pagedown escape |

### chan.lfo

A number that swings up and down by itself (sine, triangle, square, saw): regular motion, pulsing, blinking

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rate` | float | `1` | 0.01 to 100 Hz (soft) | Full waves per second: 1 Hz is one up and down each second, 0.1 one every ten seconds |
| `shape` | sine \| triangle \| square \| saw | `"sine"` |  | The form of one wave, from -1 to 1 before amplitude and offset; sine: smoothly up and down, slow at the turns; triangle: straight up and straight down at an even speed; square: 1 for the first half of each wave, -1 for the second, jumping between; saw: rising evenly from -1 to 1, then jumping back |
| `amplitude` | float | `1` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Half the swing: the value goes from offset - amplitude to offset + amplitude |
| `offset` | float | `0` | -1 to 1 (soft) | The centre the wave swings around; 0.5 with amplitude 0.5 gives 0 to 1 |
| `phase` *(more)* | float | `0` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Shift along the wave, in waves: 0.25 is a quarter wave ahead. Sets lfos of one rate apart |
| `name` | text | `"value"` |  | Name of the channel it makes, as bindings and other nodes see it |

### chan.math

Calculates with channels: adds, multiplies or compares two inputs, or one input and a number

Inputs:

- `a` (chan)
- `b` (chan): Each channel of a meets b's channel of the same name, else b's first channel. Unconnected: the param `b`

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | add \| subtract \| multiply \| divide \| min \| max \| power \| modulo \| floor \| equal | `"add"` |  | What is done with a and b, sample by sample; add: a + b; subtract: a - b; multiply: a times b: b scales a; divide: a divided by b; min: the smaller of a and b: b is a ceiling; max: the larger of a and b: b is a floor; power: a to the power b; modulo: a wrapped into 0 to b (b = 0 leaves a); floor: a down to a multiple of b (b = 1: whole numbers; b = 0 leaves a); equal: 1 where a equals b (to within a millionth), else 0: whether the piece channel is 3 |
| `b` | float | `0` | -1 to 1 (soft) | The b side as a number, used while input b is unconnected |

### chan.merge

Puts the channels of up to four inputs together into one

Inputs:

- `a` (chan)
- `b` (chan)
- `c` (chan)
- `d` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

### chan.mouse_in

The mouse pointer and its buttons as channels, anywhere on the desktop: steer or trigger things by hand during a show

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): `x`, `y`: the pointer as shares of the display, 0 to 1 from the bottom left (`y` 1 at the top); `inside`: 1 while it is on that display; `left`, `right`, `middle`: 1 while held; `wheel`: notches turned anywhere, summed (up positive)

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | text |  |  | The display `x` and `y` are shares of, named as an output's `display` (or `\\.\DISPLAY2`); empty: the display the pointer is on |

### chan.noise

A number that wanders smoothly at random: organic motion that never repeats

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frequency` | float | `1` | 0.01 to 50 Hz (soft) | How fast the noise wanders: about this many rises and falls per second |
| `amplitude` | float | `1` | 0 to 2 (soft) | Half the swing: the value stays within about offset - amplitude to offset + amplitude |
| `offset` | float | `0` | -1 to 1 (soft) | The centre the noise wanders around |
| `seed` | int | `0` | 0 to 100 (soft) | Picks another motion of the same character; one seed always gives the same motion |
| `octaves` *(more)* | int | `2` | 1 to 8 | How much fine wiggle rides on the motion: 1 is smoothest. Each octave adds a layer at twice the frequency of the one before |
| `roughness` *(more)* | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Strength of each octave relative to the one before; higher is more jittery |
| `name` | text | `"value"` |  | Name of the channel it makes, as bindings and other nodes see it |

### chan.null

Passes its input on unchanged: a fixed point to look at, or to bind params to while the chain before it changes

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

### chan.osc_in

OSC from apps, controllers and other programs (TouchOSC on a phone, say): every address a channel

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): A channel per address (per number), holding its latest value
- `messages` (table): What arrived: address, count, values

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `port` | int | `8000` | 1024 to 65535 (soft) | UDP port to listen on; osc.status says which port it got; 0: any free port |
| `lan` | bool | `false` |  | Also take OSC from other devices (phones, other computers): listens on every network interface. Off: this machine only |
| `addresses` | text | `"*"` |  | Space-separated OSC patterns of the addresses to keep as channels: `/1/* /xy`; `*` all; `^/ping` leaves an address out |
| `params` | bool | `false` |  | Also set the params the addresses name: `/scene/speed 0.5` sets /scene.speed (live, outside the undo history). For continuous control, bind params to the channels instead |

### chan.osc_out

Sends channels and table rows as OSC to another program or device

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs:

- `chans` (chan)
- `table` (table)

Outputs: none.

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | text | `"127.0.0.1"` |  | IP address to send to, or localhost; names are not looked up |
| `port` | int | `9000` | 1024 to 65535 (soft) | UDP port the receiver listens on (TouchOSC and many apps use 9000) |
| `rate` | float | `30` | 1 to 120 Hz (soft) | Sends per second at most |
| `send` | changes \| always | `"changes"` |  | Which channels each send carries; changes: only what changed, plus everything once a second; always: everything, each time |
| `prefix` | text |  |  | Put before every channel's address: `/show` sends /show/x |
| `bundle` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | Several messages per packet as a bundle; off sends one packet per message |

### chan.out

An output port of the component this node sits in: what is wired into this node comes out of that port outside

Inside a component: one of its outputs.

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

### chan.rename

Renames channels by `from=to` pairs, so they match what other nodes and bindings expect

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | text |  |  | Space-separated `from=to` pairs, the first match wins: `tx=x ty=y`. With one `*` on each side the matched part carries over: `pos*=p*` makes pos_a into p_a |

### chan.select

Picks some of the input's channels by name or pattern, in the order given

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | text | `"*"` |  | Space-separated names, `*` matches any run of characters: `x y pos*`; `^name` leaves channels out. To rename, add a chan.rename |

### chan.sequence

A timed show: pieces one after another with cuts, fades, dips to black and flashes. Drives the tex.sequence that shows it, and a run channel per piece

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over. Cooks in every frame, whether anything shows it or not, so it sees every change of its params.

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): `seconds` into the show (loop: into the round), `step` (counted from 0; -1 in the lead-in, the number of steps after the last), `piece` (the step's piece number, -1 for none), `from`, `to` and `mix` (the entries shown: a piece number, -1 black, -2 white; mix is the share of `to`, 0 while one entry shows), `done` (1 once the show has played through), `length` (the show's seconds) and `run_<name>` per piece: 1 while it is shown, also during its fades

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | text |  |  | One step per line: piece, seconds, transition into the next step, its length. E.g. `faces 10 fade 2`. Transitions: cut, fade (cross-fade over the step's last seconds), black (fade out to black, the next cuts in), flash (cut to white, which fades into the next step over its first seconds). # starts a comment. The last step's transition leads into the black the show ends in |
| `file` | file (json, txt) |  |  | Read the steps from this file instead (relative to the project directory; saving it reloads): lines as in `steps`, or JSON {"lead_in": s, "steps": [{"piece", "duration", "transition", "length"}]}, whose lead_in then wins over the param |
| `names` | text |  |  | The pieces in input order, separated by spaces: piece k is input in<k> of a tex.sequence and has a channel run_<name>. Steps naming another piece are left out. Empty: the pieces in the order the steps first name them |
| `lead_in` | float | `1` | 0 to 10 s (soft) | Black before the first step, so its piece starts over when the show starts |
| `run` | float | `1` | 0 to 1 (soft) | On from 0.5 up (with `equals` set: while it equals that number). Each time it turns on the show starts from its beginning; while it is off it shows black and every run gate is 0 |
| `equals` | int | `-1` (off) | -1 to 20 (soft) | When set, `run` is on while it equals this number: bind `run` to the channel that says which piece plays and set this to the show's own number. While off, `run` is on from 0.5 up; -1: off |
| `mode` | once \| loop | `"once"` |  | What the show does after its last step; once: it ends in black and stays there; loop: it starts over from its lead-in, round after round |

### chan.spacemouse_in

The 3D mouse (SpaceNavigator) as channels: six axes and two buttons, to steer things by hand during a show

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): -1 to 1 each: `right` (slide the cap right), `up` (lift it), `forward` (push it away), `pitch` (tilt it, nose up), `yaw` (twist it clockwise), `roll` (tilt it sideways, to the right); `button_left`, `button_right`: 1 while held; `connected`: 1 while the device is there

### chan.speed

Turns a speed into a position: adds up each channel over time, for steady turning, scrolling or drifting

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (chan)

Outputs: `out` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | none \| loop \| clamp | `"none"` |  | Whether the sum is kept within min and max; none: the sum grows without end; loop: past max it starts again from min (and the other way round): an angle, a scroll; clamp: the sum stops at min and max |
| `min` | float | `0` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Lower end of the range the sum stays in (limit loop or clamp) |
| `max` | float | `1` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Upper end of the range the sum stays in (limit loop or clamp) |
| `reset` | bool | `false` |  | Hold the sum at 0 (or min) while on |

### chan.trail

Records the recent past of each channel: a graph over time to look at, or a history to work with

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves. Keeps state from frame to frame. `node.reset`, the reset button or R starts the node over.

Inputs:

- `in` (chan): The channels to record. Of each channel the trail takes its current value (the last sample)

Outputs:

- `out` (chan): The input's channels by name, the newest sample last. The trail starts with one sample (when made, reset or sought back) and grows by one per sample taken, up to length times rate

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | float | `5` | 0.1 to 60 s (soft) | How far back the trail reaches once it is full; older values drop off its start |
| `rate` | float | `60` | 1 to 240 Hz (soft) | Samples taken per second of show time, whatever the frame rate; length times rate is the number of samples of a full trail |
| `active` | bool | `true` |  | Records while on. Off holds the trail as it is; recording resumes from the moment active is on again |

## geo

[geo.assign_material](#geoassign_material), [geo.file](#geofile), [geo.instance](#geoinstance), [geo.merge](#geomerge), [geo.primitive](#geoprimitive), [geo.tex_instance](#geotex_instance), [geo.transform](#geotransform)

### geo.assign_material

Gives geometry a material: how it looks when rendered

Inputs:

- `in` (geo)
- `mat` (mat)

Outputs: `out` (geo).

### geo.file

A 3D model from a file (OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB) with its parts; updates when the file changes

Inputs: none.

Outputs:

- `out` (geo): The mesh
- `parts` (table): One row per part: id, name, triangles, bounds (min_x .. max_z)

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | file (obj, stl, gltf, glb) |  |  | The mesh file, relative to the project directory; saving it again reloads the node |
| `up` *(more)* | auto \| y \| z | `"auto"` |  | Which axis is up in the file, turned into penumbra's z up; auto: y for glTF and OBJ, z for STL; y: the file's y is up (most modelling tools, glTF); z: the file's z is up already, as STL from CAD usually is |
| `normals` | file \| smooth | `"file"` |  | Which way each corner faces, for the shading; file: as the file has them (flat where it has none, as STL); smooth: averaged over each corner's faces, for faceted or voxel meshes |
| `rings` *(more)* | int | `1` | 1 to 16 | smooth: rings of faces averaged around each corner; 3 to 6 for voxel or marching-cubes meshes |
| `crease` *(more)* | float | `180` | 0 to 180° | smooth: edges sharper than this stay hard; 180 smooths everything |

### geo.instance

Many copies of a model, each placed by a row of a table: a grid, a ring, a crowd of objects

Inputs:

- `in` (geo)
- `table` (table): One row per copy. The first row names the columns: tx ty tz to move, rx ry rz to turn (degrees), sx sy sz to scale

Outputs:

- `out` (geo): The copies; part ids continue from copy to copy

### geo.merge

Combines several pieces of geometry into one, to render them together

Inputs:

- `in0` (geo)
- `in1` (geo)
- `in2` (geo)
- `in3` (geo)
- `in4` (geo)
- `in5` (geo)
- `in6` (geo)
- `in7` (geo)

Outputs:

- `out` (geo): All inputs as one; part ids continue from input to input

### geo.primitive

A simple shape: a box, a sphere or a plane, centred on the origin

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (geo).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | box \| sphere \| plane | `"box"` |  | Which shape, centred on the origin; size sets its measures; box: a cuboid of size x by y by z; sphere: a ball as wide as size x; plane: an upright rectangle facing -y, size x wide and size z high |
| `size` | vec3 | `[1, 1, 1]` | 0 to 10 (soft) | Box: x, y, z; sphere: the diameter is x; plane (upright, facing -y): x wide, z high |
| `segments` *(more)* | int | `48` | 3 to 128 (soft) | Steps around the sphere (half as many from pole to pole); more is rounder and costs more |
| `cells` | int | `1` | 1 to 128 (soft) | Plane: quads along each side; with mat.wireframe a grid of lines (a floor to fly over) |

### geo.tex_instance

Thousands of copies of a model, placed, scaled, turned and coloured by pictures, all on the GPU: particles, swarms

Inputs:

- `in` (geo)
- `position` (tex): One texel per copy: copy i reads texel (i % width, i / width). Its rgb moves the copy (x, y, z in metres)
- `aim` (tex): Its rgb turns the copy's +y towards that direction, keeping +z up
- `scale` (tex): Its rgb scales the copy per axis
- `color` (tex): Its rgb multiplies the copy's colour

Outputs: `out` (geo).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extent` *(more)* | float | `10` | 0.1 to 1000 (soft) | Half the side of a box around the origin that holds every copy. Framing and shadow maps use this box, since the positions stay on the GPU |

### geo.transform

Moves, turns and scales geometry (scale first, then rotate, then move)

Inputs:

- `in` (geo)

Outputs: `out` (geo).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translate` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Move along x, y, z (z up), in scene units (metres), after scale and rotate |
| `rotate` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -180 to 180° (soft) | Turn about x, then y, then z, after scale and before translate |
| `scale` | vec3 | `[1, 1, 1]` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Size along x, y, z around the origin, applied first: 1 keeps the size, negative mirrors |
| `uniform` | float | `1` | 0.001 to 1000 (soft) | Times the scale: 0.001 turns millimetres into metres |

Invisible, but hides what is behind it: a real object in front of a projection; casts shadows

### mat.pbr

A realistic surface, metal or plastic, rough or glossy, lit by the render's lights; best with a light.environment

Inputs:

- `texture` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (mat).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear RGBA, straight alpha; replaces the file's colour; times the texture input |
| `metallic` | float | `0` | 0 to 1 | 0: plastic, paint, glass; 1: metal, whose colour tints its reflections |
| `roughness` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 | 0: a mirror; 1: matte |
| `emit` *(more)* | colour | `[0, 0, 0, 1]` |  | Light the surface gives off by itself; alpha is unused |
